context.process_name: Two-Ledger Allocation Framework (Capital vs Carry Interest)
context.objective: Document how we carry out Two-Ledger Allocation Framework (Capital vs Carry Interest), the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we confirm event and authority. That is done by: GPFS Preparer. Before starting we need approved event total or upstream amount. What we do: identify the event and governing basis; create separate capital and carry sections; record the source period and calculation purpose.
What event or notification prompts the preparer to begin this work?

Next, we lock population and schedules. That is done by: GPFS Preparer; client confirms. Before starting we need current schedules, prior member population, and  and changes. What we do: reconcile the changes; confirm effective dates and the components covered; freeze the dated approved versions.
What do you reconcile the population changes against before freezing the schedules?

After that, we calculate capital-interest ledger. That is done by: GPFS Preparer. Before starting we need approved allocation method and reconciled contributions. What we do: use the approved whole-population, deal, or tranche basis; isolate contributions for realized events; calculate the capital components; independently reconcile the sources and formulas.
What determines whether you use the whole-population, deal, or tranche basis?

Then, we calculate carry-interest ledger. That is done by: GPFS Preparer. Before starting we need approved carry base, schedules, and carry recorded in prior periods. What we do: calculate each applicable schedule on a life-to-date basis; subtract all carry recorded in prior periods; apply approved changes.
What approved changes do you apply to the carry calculation?

Once that is done, we combine and analyze. That is done by: GPFS Preparer; Reviewer. Before starting we need completed component ledgers. What we do: combine the results by member; reconcile the components with the event total; explain results that move in different directions; obtain client confirmation when the intended result is unclear.

notes.summary: The preparer and reviewer combine completed ledgers by member, reconcile components to the event total and explain results moving in different directions. They obtain client confirmation when the intended result is unclear. The final completion condition remains open.

topics.answer: The work is called “Two-Ledger Allocation Framework (Capital vs Carry Interest).”

Before starting, the GPFS Preparer needs an approved event total or an upstream amount.
The actual initiating event, who receives or detects it, and the work’s cadence or fixed deadline have not been established.
The observable finished condition and any steps following combination and analysis have not been established.

The GPFS Preparer performs the initial event and authority confirmation and setup, and the subsequent population and schedules step; the client confirms in the latter step.
The role accountable for the completed result, distinct from the GPFS Preparer’s stated actions, is not established.

At the beginning, the GPFS Preparer identifies the event and governing basis, creates separate capital and carry sections, and records the source period and calculation purpose.
Next, the GPFS Preparer locks population and schedules, with client confirmation. The step requires current schedules, the prior member population and changes; the preparer reconciles changes, confirms effective dates and components covered, and freezes dated approved versions.
After locking population and schedules, the GPFS Preparer calculates the capital-interest ledger using an approved allocation method and reconciled contributions. The preparer uses the approved whole-population, deal or tranche basis, isolates contributions for realized events and calculates capital components; sources and formulas are independently reconciled.
After the capital-interest ledger, the GPFS Preparer calculates the carry-interest ledger. The preparer calculates each applicable schedule life to date, subtracts all carry recorded in prior periods, and applies approved changes.
After both component ledgers are completed, the GPFS Preparer and Reviewer combine results by member, reconcile the components with the event total, explain results moving in different directions and obtain client confirmation when the intended result is unclear.

The initial step is to confirm the event and authority.
How the event and authority are confirmed, what evidence is checked or retained, and what happens if confirmation fails are not established.
For population and schedules, the GPFS Preparer reconciles changes and confirms effective dates and components covered; the client confirms, and dated approved versions are frozen.
The precise subject and mechanism of client confirmation, approval of the versions, and handling of discrepancies are not established.
The capital-interest calculation includes an independent reconciliation of sources and formulas.
The inputs compared when reconciling population changes, and the mechanism and performer of the independent sources-and-formulas reconciliation, remain unspecified.
The combine-and-analyze step reconciles the components to the event total and explains results moving in different directions. Client confirmation is obtained when the intended result is unclear; the stated participants are the GPFS Preparer and Reviewer.
The respective preparer and reviewer responsibilities, reconciliation failure handling and evidence of the conditional client confirmation remain unspecified.

The capital calculation can use an approved whole-population, deal or tranche basis.
The circumstances and reasons for choosing each allocation basis, and how the resulting work differs, remain unspecified.

Current schedules, the prior member population and changes are inputs to locking population and schedules; dated approved versions are frozen.
An approved event total or upstream amount is needed for the initial confirmation and setup.
The capital-interest calculation requires an approved allocation method and reconciled contributions as inputs.
The carry-interest calculation requires an approved carry base, schedules and carry recorded in prior periods.
Completed capital and carry component ledgers are inputs to the member-level combination and analysis.

The initial setup identifies the governing basis for the event and records the source period and calculation purpose.
The specific governing basis, its source, and how it determines the capital-versus-carry treatment have not been established.
The population and schedules step uses effective dates and components covered and freezes dated approved versions.
The capital-interest calculation uses the approved whole-population, deal or tranche basis and isolates contributions for realized events.
How the applicable allocation basis is selected and how capital components are calculated from the contributions remain unspecified.
For carry interest, each applicable schedule is calculated life to date, all carry recorded in prior periods is subtracted, and approved changes are applied.
The calculation of each carry schedule, selection of applicable schedules, and application of approved changes remain unspecified.
When the intended result is unclear during combination and analysis, client confirmation is obtained.

steps.title: Confirm event and authority

steps.description: Create separate capital and carry sections.

steps.description: Record the source period and calculation purpose.

steps.title: Reconcile population changes
steps.description: Reconcile changes as part of locking the population and schedules. The client confirms this stage, but the precise subject and timing of that confirmation are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Confirm dates and components
steps.description: Confirm effective dates and the components covered as part of locking population and schedules.

steps.title: Freeze approved versions
steps.description: Freeze the dated approved versions. Who approves the versions and how approval is established are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Apply approved allocation basis
steps.description: Use the approved whole-population, deal, or tranche basis and isolate contributions for realized events.

steps.title: Calculate capital components
steps.description: Calculate the capital components using the approved allocation basis and reconciled contributions.

steps.title: Independently reconcile sources and formulas
steps.description: Independently reconcile the sources and formulas used in the capital-interest ledger.

steps.title: Calculate carry schedules life to date
steps.description: Calculate each applicable carry schedule on a life-to-date basis. Before starting this carry-ledger work, an approved carry base, schedules, and carry recorded in prior periods are needed.

steps.title: Subtract prior-period carry
steps.description: Subtract all carry recorded in prior periods.

steps.title: Apply approved carry changes
steps.description: Apply approved changes to the carry calculation. The changes and their application are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Combine results by member
steps.description: Combine the completed capital and carry component ledgers by member. The individual responsibilities of the preparer and reviewer are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Reconcile components to event total
steps.description: Reconcile the components with the event total. The respective preparer and reviewer responsibilities and discrepancy handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Explain differing result directions
steps.description: Explain results that move in different directions. The respective preparer and reviewer responsibilities are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Obtain client confirmation
steps.description: Obtain client confirmation when the intended result is unclear. Who requests it, how the client responds, and what follows confirmation are UNKNOWN.
